title: Behavioral Messages and Debt Repayment
The development revolution will not be nudged: The c2-frame approach as a proposal
Environmental justice beyond race: Skin tone and exposure to air pollution
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract:
Recent research, focused mostly on the United States andWestern Europe, shows that marginalized communities often face greater environmental degradation. However, the ethnoracial categories used in these studies may not fully capture environmental inequality in the Global South. Moving beyond conventional ethnoracial variables, this study presents novel findings exploring the link between skin tone and fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure in Colombia. By matching household geolocations from a large-scale longitudinal survey with satellite-based PM2.5 estimates, we find that skin tone predicts both initial pollution exposure levels and their changes over time.
Although average exposure levels remained stable during our study period, the environmental justice (EJ) landscape in Colombia contemporaneously underwent a complete transformation. In 2010, lighter-skinned individuals faced higher PM2.5 exposure, but darker-skinned individuals experienced steeper increases in the following years. By
2016, the EJ gap had reversed, with people with the darkest skin tones exposed to PM2.5 levels nearly one standard deviation higher than those faced by people with the lightest skin tones. These patterns remain robust when controlling for a comprehensive set of theoretically relevant covariates, including ethnoracial self-identification and income. Disproportionate exposure to pollution from fires partially explains the observed disparities. Decomposition analysis shows that this variable, local collective action, and economic marginalization account for a sizeable share of the EJ gap. However, one-third of the gap remains unexplained by observable characteristics. With climate change intensifying fire incidence, the disproportionate disease burdens that vulnerable groups face might deepen unless policy measures are taken to reverse this trend.
abstract_zh:
近期研究主要集中在美国和西欧，表明边缘化社区往往面临更严重的环境退化。然而，这些研究所使用的种族与民族类别可能无法充分反映全球南方的环境不平等。本研究超越了传统的种族与民族变量，首次探讨了哥伦比亚肤色与细颗粒物（PM2.5）暴露之间的联系。通过将大规模纵向调查中的家庭地理位置与基于卫星的PM2.5估计值相匹配，我们发现肤色既能预测初始污染暴露水平，也能预测其随时间的变化。
尽管在研究期间平均暴露水平保持稳定，哥伦比亚的环境正义（EJ）格局在同一时期经历了彻底的转变。2010年，肤色较浅的个体面临更高的PM2.5暴露，但肤色较深的个体在随后几年经历了更陡峭的上升。到2016年，环境正义差距发生了逆转：肤色最深的人群所暴露的PM2.5水平，比肤色最浅的人群高出近一个标准差。在控制一整套理论上相关的协变量（包括种族与民族自我认同和收入）后，这些格局依然稳健。来自火灾的污染暴露不均衡部分解释了所观察到的差异。分解分析表明，该变量、当地集体行动和经济边缘化共同解释了环境正义差距的相当大一部分。然而，差距中仍有三分之一无法由可观测特征解释。随着气候变化加剧火灾发生率，除非采取政策措施扭转这一趋势，弱势群体所承受的不成比例的疾病负担可能会进一步加深。

title: Breaking the elected rules in a field experiment on forestry resources
Distance friction and the cost of hunting in tropical forest
abstract: Empirical studies of tropical forest hunting have shown the existence of marked spatial gradients of hunting effort, game harvest, and animal abundance, as hunters mostly hunt near villages, roads, and rivers. The mechanisms underlying these patterns have, however, hitherto been poorly known. This article presents a spatial bioeconomic model based on the concept of distance friction, i.e. an increasing marginal cost of distance. The model is validated by comparison with an economic field experiment with Amazonian hunters and with previous empirical data on hunting.
abstract_zh: 关于热带森林狩猎的实证研究表明，狩猎努力、猎物捕获量和动物丰度存在明显的空间梯度，因为猎人大多在村庄、道路和河流附近狩猎。然而，这些格局背后的机制此前鲜为人知。本文提出了一个基于“距离摩擦”（distance friction）概念的空间生物经济模型，即距离的边际成本递增。该模型通过与亚马逊猎人的经济实地实验以及先前的狩猎实证数据进行比较，得到了验证。
